intro: Welcome back! Now that you know numbers to 100, let's use them for time: the days of the week, the months, clock times and dates like the seventeenth of August. Warm-up: what day is it today?
teachingNotes: Days and months always start with a capital letter (Monday, May). Prepositions: on + day or date (on Monday, on the fifth of May), in + month (in May), at + clock time (at seven o'clock). Indonesian speakers often say 'in Monday' or 'on May'.

'Setengah tujuh' is 6:30, which is HALF PAST SIX in English. Never translate it as 'half seven' — in British English 'half seven' means 7:30, the opposite. 'Half past six' and the digital 'six thirty' are always safe.

Teach o'clock, quarter past, half past, quarter to, and the digital style for any other time (seven fifteen, seven forty). 'A quarter past' and 'quarter past' are both fine. Indonesia writes 19.00; in speech English uses 'seven p.m.' or 'seven in the evening', not 'nineteen'.

Dates use ordinal numbers, not cardinals: the first of May, not 'the one of May'. Special forms: first, second, third, fifth, eighth, ninth, twelfth, twentieth; most others add -th. 'The first of May' and 'May the first' are both fine; written 1 May or May 1.
Limits: grammar only through fixed chunks (What time is it? It's… / The meeting is on… at… / When is your birthday? It's on…). No past tense, no years, no 'twenty-five to' style times.

keyPoints.title: Days and months
keyPoints.explanation: Days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Months: January to December. Always use a capital letter. Use on with days and in with months.

keyPoints.title: Telling the time
keyPoints.explanation: Ask 'What time is it?' and answer 'It's…'. Full hours: o'clock. Then quarter past (:15), half past (:30), quarter to (:45) — or just say the numbers (seven fifteen). Setengah tujuh = 6:30 = half past six.

keyPoints.title: Ordinal numbers and dates
keyPoints.explanation: first, second, third, fourth, fifth… Dates use them: the first of May, or May the first. Use on with dates.

examples.en: Independence Day is on the seventeenth of August.
My birthday is on the fifth of June.

blocks.text: English days and months always start with a **capital letter**. All the days end in **-day**. Use **on** with days (*on Monday*) and **in** with months (*in May*).

id.text: Nama hari dan bulan dalam bahasa Inggris selalu diawali **huruf kapital**. Semua nama hari berakhiran **-day**. Pakai **on** untuk hari (*on Monday*) dan **in** untuk bulan (*in May*).

rows.note: say WENZ-day; the first d is silent

blocks.text: **on** Monday, **in** May. Not *in Monday* or *on May*. Days are short (one day) → on; months are long → in.

id.text: **on** Monday, **in** May. Bukan *in Monday* atau *on May*. Hari itu pendek (satu hari) → on; bulan itu panjang → in.

blocks.explain: January, February, March, April. Maret → April.

id.explain: January, February, March, April. Maret → April.

blocks.text: Ask **What time is it?** and answer **It's** + the time. On the hour, say **o'clock**: *It's seven o'clock*. For other times, **past** means after the hour and **to** means before the next hour: **quarter past seven** (7:15), **half past seven** (7:30), **quarter to eight** (7:45). The easy way for any time: just say the numbers — **seven fifteen**, **seven thirty**, **seven forty**.

id.text: Tanyakan **What time is it?** dan jawab **It's** + jamnya. Untuk jam tepat, katakan **o'clock**: *It's seven o'clock*. Untuk waktu lain, **past** berarti lewat dari jam itu dan **to** berarti kurang dari jam berikutnya: **quarter past seven** (7:15), **half past seven** (7:30), **quarter to eight** (7:45). Cara mudah untuk jam berapa pun: sebut saja angkanya — **seven fifteen**, **seven thirty**, **seven forty**.

blocks.text: Careful! **Setengah tujuh** is 6:30 = **half past six**. Indonesian counts the half *towards* the next hour; English counts it *past* the hour you just passed. Don't say *half seven* — in British English that means 7:30!

id.text: Hati-hati! **Setengah tujuh** itu 6:30 = **half past six**. Bahasa Indonesia menghitung setengah *menuju* jam berikutnya; bahasa Inggris menghitungnya *lewat* dari jam sebelumnya. Jangan bilang *half seven* — dalam bahasa Inggris British itu berarti 7:30!

blocks.text: In Indonesia you often see **19.00**. In English people usually say **seven p.m.** or **seven in the evening**, and **a.m.** for the morning: *7 a.m.* = seven in the morning.

id.text: Di Indonesia kamu sering melihat **19.00**. Dalam bahasa Inggris orang biasanya bilang **seven p.m.** atau **seven in the evening**, dan **a.m.** untuk pagi: *7 a.m.* = jam tujuh pagi.

blocks.explain: 2:30 is thirty minutes past two, so half past two. 'Half three' means 3:30 in British English.

id.explain: 2:30 itu tiga puluh menit lewat jam dua, jadi half past two. 'Half three' berarti 3:30 dalam bahasa Inggris British.

blocks.text: For dates, English uses **ordinal numbers** (first, second, third…), not *one, two, three*. Say **the first of May** or **May the first**. Most ordinals just add **-th**: fourth, sixth, tenth. Learn the special ones: **first, second, third, fifth, eighth, ninth, twelfth, twentieth**. Use **on** with dates.

id.text: Untuk tanggal, bahasa Inggris memakai **bilangan urutan** (first, second, third…), bukan *one, two, three*. Katakan **the first of May** atau **May the first**. Sebagian besar cukup ditambah **-th**: fourth, sixth, tenth. Hafalkan yang khusus: **first, second, third, fifth, eighth, ninth, twelfth, twentieth**. Pakai **on** untuk tanggal.

rows.id: kedua puluh satu · ketiga puluh satu

rows.en: Independence Day is on the seventeenth of August.
Kartini Day is on the twenty-first of April.
My birthday is on the fifth of June.

blocks.text: Indonesian says *tanggal satu*, but English needs the ordinal: **the first of May**, never *the one of May*. Written, it's **1 May** or **May 1**, but you still say *the first*.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia bilang *tanggal satu*, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh bilangan urutan: **the first of May**, jangan *the one of May*. Ditulis **1 May** atau **May 1**, tapi tetap dibaca *the first*.

blocks.prompt: How do you say the date 2 March?
blocks.explain: Dates use ordinals: 2 → second. 'The two of March' is the common mistake.

id.explain: Tanggal memakai bilangan urutan: 2 → second. 'The two of March' adalah kesalahan yang umum.

blocks.text: Now put it together: **on** + day or date, **at** + time. Say the day first, then the time: *The meeting is on Monday at nine o'clock.*

id.text: Sekarang gabungkan: **on** + hari atau tanggal, **at** + jam. Sebut harinya dulu, lalu jamnya: *The meeting is on Monday at nine o'clock.*

rows.en: What day is it today? — It's Wednesday.
rows.id: Hari ini hari apa? — Hari Rabu.

rows.en: The meeting is on Monday at nine o'clock.
The English class is on Friday at half past three.
rows.id: Kelas bahasa Inggrisnya hari Jumat jam setengah empat.

rows.en: The concert is on Saturday, the twentieth of December.

blocks.text: Three little words: **on** for days and dates, **in** for months, **at** for clock times.

id.text: Tiga kata kecil: **on** untuk hari dan tanggal, **in** untuk bulan, **at** untuk jam.

suggestedQuestions: Why is 'setengah tujuh' half past six and not half seven?
When do I use on, in and at with time?
How do I say a time like 19.00 in English?

Kapan pakai on, in dan at untuk waktu?
Bagaimana mengucapkan jam 19.00 dalam bahasa Inggris?
Bilangan urutan mana saja yang tidak beraturan?
